div.div: سُيُوفٌ سُرَيْجِيَّةٌ , (O, K,) or سُرَيْجِيَّاتٌ, (As, S,) Certain swords so called in relation to a blacksmith named سُرَيْجٌ: (As, S, O, K:) or they may be so called because having much water, and [glistening] wavy marks or streaks or grain. (Ham p. 326.) [See also مُسَرَّجٌ.]
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
